chapter: Mutes, influences and the blues singers
title: Bessie Smith versus Clara Smith: rival shows and the club showdown
summary: When two Smith shows were booked into the same town, the rivals sat at named tables in a club and tried to outdo each other while the master of ceremonies chose who to introduce first.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: Not her sister, but I mean anybody else who moved in, you know. Oh, you would like this. Bessie, Clara, the two -- lot of people thought they were sisters. But they'd be booked into the same town, quite often. You know, the guys would be booking, put Bessie in this theater, and Clara in the other theater across town, you know, up or the street, and the people would, you know, the towns were small. There would be -- have to divide the crowd, instead of the agent, you know, the agents are greedy. Instead of waiting if they'd had to have had a brain, they would wait and use one blues singer little segment, one guy trying to outdo the other.

So -- and while they was -- both theaters going, trying to get a crowd, trying to clean the town, they always had a club in all those towns, nightclubs. It would send an invitation, Miss Bessie Smith, you and your company are cordially invited to our club. Thursday night, wherever, so he said (unintelligible) so- and-so please come, you know. And do the same thing to Clara.

Now, both of them had shows. Clara had a show with 25, 30 people. The other would have 25 or 30 people show, so they would get together, get together. They would do their hair, and get their dresses cleaned and pressed, and that --

best -- trying to outdo the other show. So they would come in and have a -- tables (laughs) on your left, and chairs, and the same thing on your right. This would have a name there, for Bessie Smith and Company. (Laughs.) Clara Smith and Company. So you'd know where to sit.

So the other would come in and look daggers at the other one, you know. (Laughs.) Boy! And the comedians and dancers. Now there's going to be a show put on between the two, Oh, this is battle to the finish. And Bessie would sit, naturally respected, would sit at the head of the table, and they'd bring out this liquor, sit a bottle here, and a bottle there, and ice, and fried chicken, salads, and whatnot, at each table. You know.
Man alive! (Laughs.) And they'd come in and sit in and Now at this time, Ladies and Gentlemen, (laughs) the M. C., we'd like to introduce -- now he's got to be careful which one to introduce first.
(Laughter.)
See?
Right, uh-huh.

Because should he introduce the wrong one, he's in trouble! And What do you mean? Don't you see me sitting here? I'm Bessie (Unintelligible.) 'I'm Clara, that means I'm the greatest one of all the Smith's,' you know.
So anyway, they'd get that going, and get that over

with, and they would get up, well thank you very much, and the people would applaud, and they're sitting there waiting, and looking from one side to the other. And the band would start playing, Mr. Conductor, the director, Professor, the most times, in those days, Professor, would you please play for me such and such and such? And you know. So the band started playing, and then the little girls would jump up and snatch off their robes, or what they had on on top, and they all dressed, and they all pretty under there, and they started dancing. You know?
And singing and dancing, and after that -- in other words, the show would go right down, and that (unintelligible).
Whichever one started first.

Right. Yeah. And they would go into the dances, and the comedians would come out. Then they'd go -- naturally the other group would come out now and do this, they wouldn't dare interfere, because the other show would laugh them under -- out in the woods, you see, get out, you're nothing, we're the best.

Then, now, Clara Smith, Bessie Smith would get up and say play such and such blues that way, and Bessie's (sings) Ye-e-e-s, a -- man, and that was it. People would start roaring, you know? (Laughs.) And Clara would get up with her voice. she had a beautiful voice. Clara would get up and sing four or five, I mean they would keep that going
until the very end.
Now, you go home and beat your brains out, and tell yourself, who's better? (Laughs.) You know what I mean?
Uh-huh.
You say well who's better? Did I like Clara better? Or did I like Bessie better? I did that -- you know.
Well that's a terrific way to hear them, I suppose.

I'm telling you, well that's the way they did, you know? And the musicians should of be -- the musicians with different shows, trumpet players and what -- they would be battling against each other, trying to sound better. See? Right down the line. Everybody was battling. Dancers would go out there and do something he'd never done before, trying to outdo this guy. You know?
So the whole show -- I mean everybody was -- it was all muscle, you know.
